title: Brilliant
brief: A professional vector design tool "where you and your AI agents work directly on the canvas." Agent-native design tooling is still rare, which makes this one notable.
details: Brilliant (brilliant.design) is a professional design tool built for human-plus-agent collaboration: "the professional design tool your agents already know how to drive." Point Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP agent at a real canvas — Brilliant is both an MCP server and client — and most AI edits in it already come from users' own CLI agents. The canvas is real vectors (not HTML mockups): a world-class GPU engine with liquid glass, refraction, iridescent metal, and animated shader fills, all live in the browser. Workflow: describe → get editable vectors → refine in place → export PNG, SVG, React, MP4. Design-system support includes multi-mode tokens, OKLCH ramps, and a plain-text DSL; every design is Blueprint, a published lossless 2D-vector language ~20x more token-efficient than JSON, so designs can be git-blamed and PR-reviewed like code. One-click round-trip with Figma, and an AI chat where you @-mention elements, point at positions, eyedrop colors, and switch providers/models with your own keys. Their thesis: everyone else bet the canvas is HTML/CSS; Brilliant bets the design is the contract above the code.
